title: Runtime text-to-motion for an LLM-driven character
author: Codemarchant
selftext:
I've been building [Rexclaw Companions](https://github.com/Codemarchant/rexclaw), an open-source AI voice companion with a 3D avatar (three.js + VRM), powered by the Grok realtime voice API.

Each character has a fixed library of about 20 gestures it can trigger itself through tool calls, which is limiting: ask for anything outside the list and it can only pretend.

So I wired in a runtime text-to-motion tool. When the character decides a movement isn't in its library, it calls a generate\_gesture tool with a text prompt. That goes over a local HTTP API to [Text-To-VRMA](https://github.com/Kirakun0328/text-to-vrma) by Kiratchi, which runs NVIDIA's ARDY motion model on my own GPU and hands back a VRMA animation that plays as soon as it's generated. In the video I ask for a cartwheel and a chicken dance, neither of which exists as an asset in the project.

It takes about 5 seconds per motion on an RTX 3070 (8 GB VRAM), likely much faster on better cards. I learned the model wants short captions like "A person does a cartwheel", not step-by-step choreography. Long descriptions gave much worse motions.

I'm excited to see this type of technology be used more in games for realtime character motion / NPC behaviours soon. Has anyone else tried runtime text-to-motion for NPCs?

comments.author: curious_biped_dev
comments.body: This is a great problem to solve with local models instead of a fixed library. Curious how you handle the 5 second gap while the motion generates, does the character keep talking or freeze, and do you cache generated VRMAs so a repeated request like "wave" doesn't regenerate every time? Also wondering if ARDY handles multi-step actions well or mostly single gestures.

replies.author: Codemarchant
replies.body:
It's waiting 5 seconds before speech for the tool call result currently, I found that more natural than trying some placeholder language/accepting de-sync between starting speech and gesture. It can take longer depending on how long the generated motion is, but I do think on better hardware would be much less time.

It can handle some multi-step actions in one prompt, but i find the results diminish the more complicated the prompt is / more steps of animation. 

I'm not caching played VRMA's automatically for immediate re-use, as I find you may get some dud animations you don't want to repeat. But i do save them to a library folder, and I have avatar configuration settings where you can save custom VRMA files against each avatar, so they can easily be configured to become part of the official avatars animation library to play instantly with description of when the agent should play each instead.

Outside this I did add some support for dlp3d speechtomotion system, their approach doesn't doesn't generate motions / grant autonomy to the agent for motions, but rather has a much larger library of common subtle motions (around 100) that are automatically run in the background per sentence based on keywords/super fast model call to decide if it should play relevant motion per sentence. So that fills gap between "one off" elaborate gestures and some common background ones.
